To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have derived the black hole mass fundamental plane relationship from a uniform sample of X-ray and radio emitting broad-line AGN and found that it has a weak dependence on the mass and that a tight correlation exists between the EDDington luminosity-scaled X-rays and radio luminosity for the radio-quietsubsample.

the fundamental plane is a very tight correlation between the 1 keV X-ray, 1.4 keV radio and black hole mass, with a weak dependence on the mass, which is different from some previously reported results.

the black hole mass has a very weak influence on the fundamental plane, and the radio-X-ray luminosity relationship for radio-quiet sources is consistent with the theoretical predictions from the accretions dominated X-ray model.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have obtained the first radio and X-ray luminosity relationship in the fundamental plane from a uniform AGN sample.
the radio-X-ray correlation for AGN is not a universal relation, but depends on the radio-loudness.
the radio and X-ray emissions in radio-loud and X-ray-emitting broad-line AGNs are likely to be produced by different mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radio-X-ray relation can be used as an effective tool in estimating the black hole mass for AGNs.
we can use the black hole fundamental planes to distinguish radio-quiet and -loud AGN populations.
